photo.reason: The photo shows a Native American infant in a decorated cradleboard/baby carrier with a beaded bag, labeled "Shoshone or Bannock" and taken in Pendleton, Oregon — a documentary studio photo of regional Plateau Native dress and material culture plausible for the Bannock.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white); photographic print
photo.reason: The image shows a baby in a traditional cradleboard/baby carrier, documentary-style photo captioned "Baby Papoose, Pocatello, Ida." — the museum itself hedges "Shoshone or Bannock," and Pocatello, Idaho is within traditional Shoshone-Bannock territory, so this is plausible evidence of Bannock material culture (cradleboard) and daily life.

garment.name: moccasin
garment.title: moccasin
garment.reason: A pair of beaded hide moccasins, directly attributed to a named Bannock donor from Fort Hall, Idaho — a classic Plains/Plateau-style footwear fitting the claimed culture and category.

textile.name: väska, cornhusk bag, bag
textile.title: väska, cornhusk bag, bag
textile.reason: A cornhusk twined bag with geometric hourglass motifs, made and used by Lizzie Edmo, a named Bannock woman from Fort Hall, Idaho, with leather carrying straps — a classic Plateau-tradition cornhusk/corn-husk bag used by Bannock-Shoshone people.

sculpture.title: doll, cradle, toy, doll, cradle

household.name: needle housing
household.title: needle housing
